comparisons.peer_summary: The Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive (CSRD) will replace and expand EU ESG reporting requirements starting in fiscal year 2024, with implementation delays in some member states, while the Corporate Sustainability Due Diligence Directive (CSDDD) enacted in July 2024 mandates due diligence obligations for human rights and environmental impacts starting in 2027, impacting the Firm's EU and non-EU entities.
comparisons.comparison: While the target (GS) focuses on internal governance and specific due diligence guidelines for managing sustainability risks, JPM discusses the external regulatory drivers (CSRD and CSDDD) that mandate such due diligence and reporting. JPM notes that the CSDDD imposes mandatory due diligence obligations for environmental adverse impacts, which aligns with GS's use of Environmental & Social Due Diligence Guidelines, but JPM's disclosure highlights the legislative timeline and scope expansion rather than the internal operational implementation described by GS.

sentences.text: We have also implemented the Environmental & Social Due Diligence Guidelines to guide our overall risk-based due diligence approach when evaluating relevant transactions for environmental and social risks and impacts.
In addition, in July 2024, the EU enacted the Corporate Sustainability Due Diligence Directive ("CSDDD"), which provides for phased-in requirements starting in 2027.

The CSDDD sets mandatory due diligence obligations for companies to address actual and potential human rights violations and environmental adverse impacts stemming from their own operations and business relationships, including the activities of certain companies with which they have established business relationships and also requires the adoption of company-specific climate-related transition plans.

comparisons.peer_summary: The Bank Secrecy Act requires financial institutions to establish risk-based internal controls to prevent money laundering and terrorism financing, alongside record-keeping, reporting, and due diligence obligations.
comparisons.comparison: Both disclosures describe the implementation of 'risk-based' controls and due diligence, but in different regulatory contexts. GS applies risk-based due diligence specifically to environmental and social risks for relevant transactions, whereas JPM applies risk-based internal controls to prevent money laundering and terrorism financing under the Bank Secrecy Act (BSA). Both highlight a structured, risk-oriented approach to compliance, but the subject matter (sustainability vs. anti-money laundering) differs.
